instructions:
You keep this person's website up to date. The site is theirs:
nothing you write is public until they approve it, and the site enforces that.
Workflow: site_state (see what exists, each item's version and field guide) ->
item_create / item_update / item_remove (images: an https link, or
photo_upload_link for a photo your person sent you) -> approval_request (only the ids you
changed for this request; site_check first) -> give the owner the review_url -> approval_status.
Finish the whole job first and send it as one request, then tell your person at once:
your drafts are invisible to them until you do.
Never put passwords, keys, tokens or private addresses in content; the site refuses them.
The look: theme_list (built-in looks are ready to use; the catalog has previews) ->
set the site item's theme -> theme_needs (the art and words that theme wants, and which
are missing) -> fill them -> one approval_request. Use theme_install only for a
catalog look missing from installed, or to update one.
Cards have a visibility: a private card is never shown and its name may not appear in
anything public (the site refuses it); a mention card shows its name and description only,
and an entry names it at most once in its summary and once in its body.
site_stats: who reads the site.

tools.name: site_state
tools.description: Start here. By default, `items` summarizes every item as id, kind, title, state (see `states`) and version (send it with item_update / item_remove / item_rollback). Title is the item's title, a card's name or a note's text. Send full: true for the complete item shape, including data, slug, deleted, created_at, updated_at, live_version, pending_approval and last_approval. Send ids: [...] for full items only for those ids, in normal item order; ids takes precedence over full; [] returns no items; an unknown id refuses the call with no_such_item. pending_approval is the approval it is waiting in now or null; last_approval is its most recent request and how it ended or null; an item whose last request was denied or superseded and that the owner did not ask about again is best left alone. All top-level fields stay present: `states`, `kinds`, `fields`, `site_defaults`, `release` and `update`. `update` says whether a newer release is published (available; when true also latest, security, changes, migrations, reconnect, how): tell your person in plain words and update only when they say so, following `how`. Then change items, approval_request the ids you changed, give the owner the review_url.

tools.name: item_create
tools.description: Create an item; nothing is public until the owner approves. Kinds: site: the site's standing text and layout. Exactly one, id "site"; create it once if site_state doesn't list it, then change it with item_update. entry: a dated post in one of the site's streams (its home section): with its own page (body in Markdown), or, with external_url, a listing that links to where it lives. card: a tile in the cards grid: projects, services, products. The grid's heading is the site's cards_title. note: a short dated line in the notes list (heading: the site's notes_title). data holds that kind's fields (see `fields` in site_state).

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Resending the same key returns the item already created (with replayed: true) instead of a duplicate. Use a new key for a different item.

tools.name: item_update
tools.description: Change some fields of an item; send only the fields that change. version: the item's current version (from site_state or your last write); on version_conflict, re-read and redo.

tools.name: item_remove
tools.description: Remove an item (recoverable with item_rollback). Takes effect on the site once approved.

tools.name: item_history
tools.description: Every version of an item, newest first, with who changed it and why; address_change {from, to} marks a version that changed an entry's slug (the old address redirects to the new one).

tools.name: item_rollback
tools.description: Stage an earlier version of an item as a new version. Then ask for approval.

tools.name: photo_upload_link
tools.description: For a photo file: one your person sent you, or one you have yourself (an image with a public https link can go straight into an image field instead). Returns url, which works once, for 30 minutes. Send the file to it yourself: POST multipart/form-data with fields `photo` (the file: JPEG, PNG or WebP, up to 8 MB) and `alt` (what it shows, in a few words), with header Accept: application/json; the answer has `image` (a /media path) and `alt`. If you can't send files, give the url to your person instead: they open it, pick the photo and describe it, and photo_upload_status tells you when it's done. Put `image` in an image field (hero, cover, a card's image, or ![alt](image) in a body) and `alt` in its description field. Nothing shows publicly until the owner approves an item that uses it. Shrink pictures before sending: web size, about 2400 pixels on the long side, usually under 1 MB (JPEG or WebP). Sending the original is possible, but tell your person first, plainly: bigger files use more of the free plan's limits, make pages slower and take more storage.

purpose.description: shown on the upload page, e.g. the cover for your trip post

tools.name: image_add
tools.description: For picture files you hold: give exactly one of data (one base64 picture, existing image/width/height response) or images (1 to 8 base64 pictures, response images:[{image,width,height},...] in input order). JPEG, PNG or WebP, at most 8 MB each and 8 MB decoded total. Every file is sniffed and stored by hash; all succeed or none are stored. Duplicates repeat in the answer and are stored once. Nothing shows publicly until the owner approves an item that uses it. Put each image path in an image field with an alt description. photo_upload_link still takes one file. Shrink pictures before sending: web size, about 2400 pixels on the long side, usually under 1 MB (JPEG or WebP). Sending the original is possible, but tell your person first, plainly: bigger files use more of the free plan's limits, make pages slower and take more storage.

data.description: one picture's bytes, base64 (standard or URL-safe alphabet); give data or images

images.description: 1 to 8 base64 pictures, at most 8 MB each and 8 MB decoded in total; give images or data

tools.name: photo_upload_status
tools.description: How a photo_upload_link is going: status waiting (not sent yet), done (image and alt are ready to use) or expired (ask for a new link).

tools.name: theme_list
tools.description: The site's look. Returns `my_requests` (themes this site asked the community for, each open, answered with the theme that answers it, or closed: tell your person when one is answered), `my_submissions` (looks this site shared: status, the curator's note, and, when the look claimed credit, credit: waiting, credited or not credited), `current` (the theme the site uses now, and the one waiting for approval if it differs), `installed` (themes this site has: built-in ones and ones installed from the catalog), and `catalog` (every theme you can install: name, title, type such as personal or product, description, previews to show your person, version, and author_x: the X handle of the look's maker, when the look is credited). Looks marked source: built-in are ready to use without installing. Set the site theme, then call theme_needs. Use theme_install only for a catalog look missing from installed, or to update one. Ask your person what the site is for, show them the catalog themes of that type with their previews, and let them pick.

tools.name: theme_request
tools.description: When no catalog theme fits what your person's site is for, ask the Porchsite community for one. Sent privately from this site to a queue a curator reads; nothing your person says is published. Describe the site and what it needs, in your own words, without names, addresses or anything personal. Then build with the closest theme meanwhile; theme_list's my_requests shows when it's answered. A site can file 3 a day.

type.description: what the site is for, one word or two with a dash: business, club, event, portfolio, family

title.description: a short name for the look, e.g. Small business with opening hours

description.description: what the site needs that no theme has, e.g. opening hours, a booking button, a weekly specials list

examples.description: up to 3 https links to sites your person likes the look of

tools.name: theme_install
tools.description: Install (or update) a theme from the Porchsite catalog, by name. Only catalog themes can be installed, and the download is checked against the catalog. Installing changes nothing visitors see: to use it, set the site item's theme field and ask for approval. Then call theme_needs.

tools.name: theme_create
tools.description: Make a look of your own for this site only (nobody else sees it), when no catalog theme fits and your person wants one now. Read https://get.porchsite.dev/authoring.md first. Send the whole look: manifest (template.json's fields: name, title, type, version, description, slots, art), sample (generic sample content, no real person), pages (home, entry, archive, tag, not_found as Mustache), partials (optional) and css (the stylesheet). No scripts. The site checks it against the template rules and refuses with the list of problems, or stores it. Sending the same name again replaces it (bump version). Then set the site item's theme to its name and ask for approval; your person sees it on the preview first.

tools.name: theme_submit
tools.description: Share a look this site made (theme_create) with everyone, ONLY when your person has said yes to sharing it. It goes privately to the Porchsite review queue from this site's server; the checks run again there, a curator reviews it, and the Porchsite owner decides whether it joins the public catalog. theme_list's my_submissions shows where it stands. In note: who the look is for and what it does that no catalog theme does. To credit the maker, pass author_x: their X handle (credit is an X handle and nothing else; never send a name, email or link), only if they want it; the answer's credit.instructions say what they post on X to prove it. A site can share 3 a day.

author_x.description: the maker's X handle without the @, to credit them in the catalog once verified

tools.name: theme_needs
tools.description: What a theme wants from this site, checked against the site as it stands now (your unapproved changes included). `images`: each picture slot with field, size (width x height; the shape matters), need (required, recommended, optional), purpose, alt_hint, prompt (a starting point if you make the image) and status (filled, missing, wrong shape, too small). `content`: the words and settings it reads, with what it does with each. `art`: how to make the pictures, as a designer would brief you: what to ask your person (the subject), the style, a prompt_prefix, and the steps, including the checks to run before you use any of it. Follow it. Your person may change the style. Omit name for the site's theme.

tools.name: approval_request
tools.description: Ask the owner to approve items you created, changed or removed (state new, changed, removed or removal staged in site_state). List only the ids for this request; an id with no unapproved change is refused. A newer request for an item replaces it in any older request. Returns id and review_url: give the review_url to the owner (it opens only for them, after they sign in; there is no preview link for you). Nothing goes live until they approve.

tools.name: approval_status
tools.description: Look up one approval by approval_id, or omit it for the 10 most recent. Each has review_url, status (pending: something still waits for the owner | decided) and per item: status (pending | published | changes_requested: make the edit in its note, then ask again | denied | superseded: the item changed after you asked, ask again) and note, plus the owner's decision_note.

tools.name: site_check
tools.description: Check proposed changes before approval. Default: ok, broken internal links and empty_sections, without rendering pages. Send deep: true once before approval on a new site or look change. It also checks rendered reachability (unreachable). A stop at 200 addresses or 10000 links returns crawl, ok: false and unreachable: []. Deep is heavy and can exceed Cloudflare Free CPU limits on big sites.

deep.description: Optional. Also crawl rendered links; this is a heavy check.

tools.name: site_stats
tools.description: Who reads the site: first-party visitor numbers, nothing that identifies a person; the owner, bots and test runs aren't counted. Returns `totals` (visits: one visitor on one day; views; engaged time; the typical visit; bounce_rate; multi_page_rate), `daily`, `pages` (per address: readers, typical and mean engaged time, how far down they read, landings, bounce_rate, exits), `sources` and `referring_domains`, and `tagged` (links you shared with ?src=<where>&p=<post> on the end), and `earlier` (past 90 days only the counts are kept: visits and views by month, newest first; the whole site only). Narrow to the visits that read one item with content_id, or that came from one tagged link with src and post.

days.description: the last N days, today included, 1 to 90

content_id.description: only visits that read this item (an entry's id)

src.description: only visits that came from links tagged ?src=<this>

post.description: only visits that came from links tagged ?p=<this>

include_test.description: also count test visits (your own checks, automated browsers)
